learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Chose 3 against 1.5 and 0.5, then locked it in.
observations.exploration: Never isolated gave 30 infections from ten cases, R 3. Clicked day 3: 15 infections, R 1.5. Clicked day 2: ten infections, R 1. Pressed Home on slider: day 0, zero infections, R 0.
observations.reveal: Corrected prediction to 1.5, explained three of six infectious days preserve half the spread; each earlier day removes a sixth. Day 2 is replacement knife-edge R 1. Explicitly acknowledged tested day 0 R 0. Caveated even daily spread and presymptomatic transmission.
observations.visual: Actual 1257 × 936 dark screenshot inspected. Six day columns of infection dots become crossed-out at day zero; slider and complete reveal legible.
observations.previewIsolation: No-history evaluation banner present on entry.

prediction.reason: Numerical commitment tests whether partial isolation reduces spread.

interaction.reason: Presets and slider boundary visibly change infections and R.

payoff.reason: Connects timing fraction to actual counts, boundary and model limitation.

clarity.reason: Labeled days, counts and slider communicate tested desktop sequence clearly.

transfer.reason: Earlier-day principle and applicability limit offered, without concrete new application.
transfer.evidence: Each earlier day removes a sixth; even-spread caveat.

accessibility.reason: One slider Home action is insufficient access audit.
accessibility.evidence: Keyboard Home worked for slider; focus sequence, contrast, phone, zoom and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Committed unchanged R prediction contradicted by half-rate result.

visualExplanation.reason: Daily infection columns and canceled dots carry timing mechanism.

playfulness.reason: Timing presets and endpoint slider enable reversible discovery.

practicalValue.reason: Makes timing of infection prevention concrete in toy setting.

depth.reason: Proportional reduction, replacement boundary and even-spread limitation linked.
depth.evidence: Day 3 R1.5, day 2 R1, day0 R0; reveal limits.

complexity.reason: Links fractions of infectious duration to infections and average replacement.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Track six-day fraction and average infections relative to one.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low; two presets and labeled slider.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: low: counts, fractions and simple ratios.

whyCool: Moving isolation to day zero visibly cancels every infection dot and the reveal acknowledges that exact tested boundary.
caveat: Fixed even-spread toy model; no different infectiousness timing or fresh application tested.
missingEvidence: Focus order, contrast, phone, zoom/reflow and motion not tested.
Home key on one slider does not establish full keyboard access.
effort: Approximately 2 minutes of actual browser review.
